extra.message: In resolve_pastes, the user-supplied 'filter' GraphQL argument is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string via text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'" % (filter, filter)) and passed to SQLAlchemy filter(). An attacker can break out of the string literal (e.g. filter="' OR 1=1 --") to inject arbitrary SQL and read/modify the database.

ImportPaste.mutate builds a shell command with user-controlled host/port/path/scheme and executes it via helpers.run_cmd(f'curl --insecure {url}'), which calls os.popen. strip_dangerous_characters only removes ';' and '&' in hard mode (and nothing in easy mode), leaving shell metacharacters such as '|', backticks, '$()', and newlines usable. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. host="x; id") that execute on the server.

ImportPaste.mutate constructs a URL entirely from user-supplied scheme/host/port/path arguments and instructs the server to fetch it with curl. There is no validation or allow-listing of the destination, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery to internal services/cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/).

resolve_system_debug concatenates the user-supplied 'arg' GraphQL argument directly into a shell command ('ps {}'.format(arg)) and executes it via helpers.run_cmd (os.popen), with no authentication required and no sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands, e.g. systemDebug(arg: "aux; cat /etc/passwd").

resolve_system_diagnostics passes the user-supplied 'cmd' argument to helpers.run_cmd(cmd) (os.popen). In easy mode security.allowed_cmds() returns True for any value, and in hard mode the allow-list uses startswith() which is bypassable (e.g. cmd='echo x; id'). Combined with the hardcoded admin credentials this yields unauthenticated-equivalent arbitrary command execution.

save_file() opens WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename with no sanitization. filename originates from the UploadPaste GraphQL mutation argument, so a payload like filename='../../tmp/evil' or an absolute path escapes the upload directory and writes attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations (arbitrary file write/path traversal).

The Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY are hardcoded to the literal string 'dvga' (overriding the earlier os.urandom(24) value). Because the secrets are publicly known, an attacker can forge Flask session cookies and sign/forge JWT access and refresh tokens, defeating authentication entirely.

The admin account is seeded with a password drawn from weak_passwords = ['changeme'] (random_password() at setup.py:48-50, used for the admin user at line 63). This hardcoded default credential allows attackers to authenticate as admin and reach admin-only command execution paths.
The operator account is created with the hardcoded password "password123". Known default credentials enable trivial authentication as operator.

get_identity() decodes the JWT with verify_signature:False and verify_exp:False. The token signature and expiration are never validated, so any attacker can craft an arbitrary unsigned/modified token (e.g. {"identity":"admin"}) and impersonate any user, bypassing authentication for token-protected functionality such as the 'me' query.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: UserObject.resolve_password returns the stored plaintext password whenever info.context.json.get('identity') == 'admin'. Since identity is derived from an unverified JWT (helpers.get_identity), an attacker can forge an admin token and read every user's plaintext password via the users/me queries.

User.password is stored as a plain String column and is compared directly in Login.mutate via User.query.filter_by(username=username, password=password). Passwords are never hashed, so database compromise and credential reuse are fully exposed.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: resolve_delete_all_pastes (the deleteAllPastes query) executes Paste.query.delete() with no authentication or authorization check. Any anonymous client can wipe the entire pastes table.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: EditPaste.mutate looks up a paste purely by the user-supplied id (Paste.query.filter_by(id=id)) and updates its title/content with no ownership or authorization check. Any client can modify any paste by id (Insecure Direct Object Reference).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DeletePaste.mutate deletes a paste by the user-supplied id (Paste.query.filter_by(id=id).delete()) with no ownership or authorization check. Any client can delete any paste by id (Insecure Direct Object Reference).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: CreateUser.mutate creates a new User account with no authentication or admin authorization. Any anonymous client can create accounts, enabling unauthorized account provisioning/privilege creation.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: resolve_users returns all User records (including the password field, only masked by a forgeable identity check) with no authentication or authorization. Any anonymous client can enumerate user accounts and (combined with the JWT bypass) retrieve their plaintext passwords.

format_custom_error embeds full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack), the exception traceback (traceback.format_exc), and the server-side caller file path into the GraphQL error response returned to clients. This leaks internal implementation details, file paths, and library versions to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The before_request handler set_difficulty reads the client-controlled X-DVGA-MODE header and, for any value other than 'Expert', calls helpers.set_mode('easy'), globally disabling all GraphQL protections (depth/cost limits, introspection block, operation-name allow-list, deny-list, GraphiQL guard). Any attacker can send X-DVGA-MODE: Beginner to downgrade the server's security mode on every request.

simulate_load() (invoked by the systemUpdate query) enters an unbounded while loop that sleeps up to 50 seconds (limit up to 500 iterations * 0.1s). It is reachable without authentication, so an attacker can issue many concurrent systemUpdate requests to tie up worker threads and deny service to legitimate users.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
